headline: Profit softens as loan-loss provisioning outpaces growth
summary_short: OneMain's Q2 2026 net income fell to $152M (-32.7% q/q, -9.0% y/y) and diluted EPS fell to $1.32 (-5.7% y/y) as provision for finance receivable losses rose 19.4% y/y to $610M on higher net charge-offs, even as revenue rose 6.6% y/y to $1,299M on receivables growth.
summary_long: Interest income rose 5.8% y/y to $1,417M on receivable growth and higher yield, but provision for finance receivable losses rose 19.4% y/y to $610M on higher net charge-offs (ratio 8.20%, +0.63ppt y/y) and continued receivables growth, pushing net income down 9.0% y/y to $152M and diluted EPS down 5.7% y/y to $1.32. Net finance receivables grew 5.3% y/y to $25,145M. Other expenses rose on higher operating costs, salaries, and restructuring charges, partly offset by an insurance-reserve release. The Board held its $1.05/share quarterly dividend and repurchased $32M of stock in the quarter. No quantified forward guidance was given; outlook remained qualitative.

drivers.explanation: Net income fell y/y and q/q as loan-loss provisioning and other expenses grew faster than revenue; the filing's own seasonality note (delinquencies lowest in Q1, rising through the year) partly explains the q/q step-down in profit.
Interest income increased on growth in average net receivables and an increase in yield, per the release's own comparison discussion.
Increase driven by growth in average net receivables and an increase in yield.

Provision for finance receivable losses rose on higher net charge-offs and receivables growth, while other expenses rose on operating costs, salaries, and restructuring charges, partly offset by an insurance-reserve release.
EPS fell less steeply than net income y/y (-5.7% vs -9.0%) because diluted weighted-average shares fell about 3.1% y/y on ongoing buybacks.
Increase attributed to higher net charge-offs and growth in receivables, per the release's own comparison discussion.
Growth driven by higher personal loan, auto finance, and credit card originations and account growth across the quarter.
Charge-off ratio rose alongside higher net charge-offs; the release's Seasonality section notes delinquencies are lowest in Q1 and rise through the remainder of the year.
Segment adjusted pretax income fell as higher provision and expense growth outweighed higher interest income in the non-GAAP reconciliation.
Rose as net charge-offs added back to adjusted pretax income outweighed the change in adjusted pretax income itself, per the segment's own non-GAAP reconciliation.
